top_news.title: Is MoE Routing a Huffman Code? Discovering the Frequency-Diversity Law in Chain-of-Thought
top_news.dek: Researchers identify that MoE routing functions as a Huffman code, optimizing expert allocation based on token frequency and task complexity.
top_news.brief: A new study reveals that Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing is not just a selection mechanism but an information-theoretic process. By applying the 'Frequency-Diversity Law,' the authors show that models like Phi-3.5-MoE and Gemma-4-27B-A4B dynamically route common tokens to sparse experts while reserving diverse expert committees for rare, complex tasks.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram illustrating MoE routing as a Huffman coding tree

top_news.title: Show HN: OneCLI – OSS credential gateway that keeps secrets out of AI agents
top_news.dek: OneCLI is an open-source credential gateway that prevents secret leakage by injecting API keys into AI agents at runtime.
top_news.brief: OneCLI acts as a secure intermediary between AI agents and external services. Instead of hardcoding credentials into agent configurations, developers store them in a centralized vault. The gateway then transparently injects the necessary keys during execution, ensuring agents never directly access or store sensitive secrets.
top_news.image_alt: OneCLI architecture diagram showing secret injection flow

top_news.title: AI firms want more data centers; Trump's EPA may give neighbors less say
top_news.dek: Proposed EPA rule changes could limit public input on data center siting and environmental impact assessments.
top_news.brief: The EPA is considering a rule change that would grant states greater authority to restrict or eliminate public participation in the approval process for new data centers. This shift aims to accelerate infrastructure development for AI-heavy workloads by reducing local regulatory friction.

top_news.title: Open Weights and American AI Leadership
top_news.dek: Microsoft advocates for open-weight models as a strategic foundation for American AI innovation.
top_news.brief: Drawing parallels to the 1980s open-source software movement, Microsoft argues that open-weight AI models are essential for maintaining a competitive, transparent, and secure technological ecosystem. The company suggests that shared foundations foster broader innovation across federal, scientific, and commercial sectors.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract representation of open source software architecture

top_news.title: The first known runaway AI agent - or a very bad marketing stunt?
top_news.dek: Security researchers are investigating whether a recent AI agent incident was a genuine exploit or a marketing fabrication.
top_news.brief: Analysis of a reported 'runaway' AI agent incident involving Hugging Face highlights the massive attack surface inherent in platforms that execute arbitrary code. Experts remain skeptical of the event's nature, questioning if it represents a legitimate security failure or a staged marketing stunt.

primary.title: What is Good? Extracting and Testing Implicit Theories of Literary Quality from LLM Reasoning Traces
